turnaround_reason: Concentrix, a top-two customer-experience/BPO vendor, dropped from $58 to ~$25 as the market decided generative AI would gut demand for its call-center/outsourcing core. It is deeply cheap (forward P/E ~2.1, ~25% FCF yield) with the bull case resting on AI-integrated CX services replacing lost seat-based revenue faster than feared.
bullish_points: Extraordinarily cheap: forward P/E ~2.1, EV/EBITDA ~5.3, P/B ~0.56, FCF ~$776M against a $1.5B market cap
Analyst consensus still 'buy' (7 buy / 2 hold), median target ~$30-35 vs ~$25 price (~27% upside)
Modest revenue growth returned (+1.9% YoY) with improving mix toward AI-integrated/agentic services
CEO and CFO made open-market purchases in 2026 (small but directionally supportive)
Positioned as one of two scaled global CX players — consolidation winner if the category survives
bearish_points: Core BPO is the textbook AI-disruption target; the entire de-rating is a bet on an existential question
Heavy leverage from the WebHelp deal: ~$5.5B debt, D/E ~204, ~3 turns of net debt
Big holder Groupe Bruxelles Lambert sold 6M shares (~$133M) in April — a real overhang and insider net-seller signal
Margins pressured amid restructuring; profit margin negative TTM (goodwill/amortization drag)
Basing -21% below 200d MA with 20% short interest; cheap multiple alone hasn't stopped the slide
catalyst: Evidence that AI-integrated CX revenue is additive (not just cannibalizing seats) and that revenue/margins inflect upward, plus deleveraging progress
suggested_trade: Small speculative starter only. This is a cheap-but-binary AI-disruption call; size it as a high-variance value bet, not a core position. Sept 24 print is the near-term test.
key_risk: AI erodes seat-based BPO revenue and pricing faster than AI-services growth offsets it, so FCF falls against a heavy debt load and the low multiple proves to be a value trap.
would_skip_if: Sept 24 print shows decelerating revenue or margin compression, or GBL continues selling — confirming the AI-disruption thesis.
